### 1 — Scene
A small surf-and-turf meal: grilled steak, a lobster tail with a buttery-looking topping, a short section of corn on the cob, and a few thick-cut fries.

### 2 — Vessel
A dinner plate, approximately **26 cm diameter**.  
Area = 3.14 × 13² ≈ **531 cm²**.

### 3–7 — Items, area, volume, weight, and energy
Weights below estimate **edible portions only**, excluding the lobster shell and corn cob. Heights for these items refer to the edible layer, not the entire shell or cob.

| Item | Plate area | Area × height = volume | Bulk density | Estimated weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Grilled steak | 20% | 106 × 1.4 = 148 ml | 0.98 | 145 g | 250 | 363 kcal |
| Lobster meat | 8% | 42 × 1.8 = 76 ml | 0.95 | 72 g | 100 | 72 kcal |
| Buttery topping | 1% | 5.3 × 1.5 = 8 ml | 1.0 | 8 g | 650 | 52 kcal |
| Corn kernels | 7% | 37 × 1.4 = 52 ml | 0.95 | 49 g | 100 | 49 kcal |
| Thick-cut fries | 9% | 48 × 1.3 = 62 ml | 0.65 | 40 g | 290 | 116 kcal |

### 4 — Coverage check
The edible food covers approximately **45%** of the plate. Exposed shell adds a little more coverage; much of the plate remains empty.

### 8 — Sanity check
Total estimated edible weight is **314 g**, providing approximately **650 kcal**. This is plausible for the visible steak, modest lobster portion, small corn section, and handful of fries. The steak’s fat content and the topping are the largest energy uncertainties.
